sources.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches tomorrow, November 19
sources.text: The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series heads to the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond. Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida — forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive. Grand Theft Auto VI arrives on PlayStation 5 Thursday, November 19, available at PlayStation Store. The game is set in the state of Leonida, home to the neon-soaked streets of Vice City and beyond in the biggest, most immersive evolution of the series yet. Jason grew up around grifters and crooks. After a stint in the Army trying to shake off his troubled teens, he found himself in the Keys doing what he knows best, working for local drug runners. Meeting Lucia could be the best or worst thing to ever happen to him. Jason knows how he’d like it to turn out but right now, it’s hard to tell. Lucia’s father taught her to fight as soon as she could walk, and life has been coming at her swinging ever since. Fighting for her family landed her in the Leonida Penitentiary. Sheer luck got her out but now more than anything, Lucia wants the good life her mom has dreamed of since their days in Liberty City. Instead of half-baked fantasies, Lucia is prepared to take matters into her own hands. Leonida is made up of six regions: Vice City, the Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, and Mount Kalaga. Here’s a closer look at what makes each region unique. The glamour, hustle, and greed of America captured in a single city. Each neighborhood has something to offer, from the pastel art deco hotels and bright white sands of Ocean Beach, to the bustling panaderías of Little Cuba and the bootleg brands of the Tisha-Wocka flea market, out to the VC Port, the cruise ship capital of the world. We’re a long way from the ’80s, but Vice City is still the sun and fun capital of America Life in this tropical archipelago isn’t flashy but it’s easy. Get your buzz on and pull up a deck chair but look out — you are right on the doorstep of some of the most beautiful and dangerous waters in all of America. You never know what lies beneath the surface of this primordial expanse. The gators may be the most famous attraction, but there are far deadlier predators and weirder discoveries among the mangroves. Cheap motels, shut-down attractions, and empty strip malls won’t bring the tourists back, but there’s a new economy in this once-popular vacation spot. It’s fueled by malt liquor, painkillers, and truck stop energy drinks. In the heart of Leonida, American industry and old school values still reign supreme — whatever the cost. The Allied Crystal sugar refinery provides the jobs, while the local biker gang provides almost everything else. A national landmark up against the state’s northern border, Mount Kalaga offers prime hunting, fishing, and off-road trails. In the lush surrounding backwoods, hillbilly mystics and paranoid radicals live far from the prying eyes of the government. Spanning stations including Classic Rock, Modern Hip-Hop, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latin, ‘80s, Electronic, Blues, Ballads, Talk Radio, and much more, Grand Theft Auto VI features the biggest and widest-ranging selection of in-game radio yet. Plus, for the first time ever, Grand Theft Auto VI introduces a series of on-demand podcasts for Jason and Lucia to experience beyond Leonida’s terrestrial radio, with both radio and podcasts available to listen to in vehicles and on foot through newly introduced headphones and earbuds connected to their smartphones.

sources.text: O mais novo título da série Grand Theft Auto nos leva ao estado de Leonida, até as ruas iluminadas de neon de Vice City e além. Jason e Lucia sempre souberam que as cartas não estavam a favor deles. Mas quando o que deveria ser um trabalho fácil dá errado, eles se encontram no lado mais escuro do lugar mais ensolarado da América, no meio de uma conspiração criminosa que cobre todo o estado de Leonida, forçados a depender um do outro mais do que nunca se quiserem sair vivos. Grand Theft Auto VI chega para PlayStation 5 quinta-feira, 19 de novembro, disponível na PlayStation Store. O jogo se passa no estado de Leonida, onde ficam as ruas banhadas de neon de Vice City e além, na maior e mais imersiva evolução da série até hoje. Jason cresceu rodeado de bandidos e vigaristas. Após um período no exército para tentar se livrar de sua adolescência perturbada, ele se encontra nos Keys fazendo o que faz melhor, trabalhando para traficantes de drogas locais. Conhecer Lucia pode ser a melhor ou a pior coisa que já aconteceu com ele. Jason sabe como gostaria que tudo terminasse, mas agora, é difícil prever. O pai de Lucia a ensinou a lutar desde que ela aprendeu a andar, e a vida tem vindo com tudo para cima dela desde então. Lutar por sua família a colocou na Penitenciária de Leonida. Sorte pura a livrou desta vez, mas agora mais do que qualquer coisa, Lucia deseja a vida boa com a qual sua mãe sonhava desde que moravam em Liberty City. Em vez de fantasias pela metade, Lucia está preparada para assumir o controle da situação. Leonida é composto de seis regiões: Vice City, as Leonida Keys, Grassrivers, Port Gellhorn, Ambrosia, e Mount Kalaga. Vamos conhecer o que torna cada região única. O glamour, o trabalho e a ganância da América capturados em uma única cidade. Cada bairro tem algo a oferecer, dos hóteis de art deco, cores pastel e areia branca de Ocean Beach, até as padarias de Little Cuba e as marcas falsificadas do mercadinho de Tisha-Wocka, até o VC Port, a capital mundial dos navios de cruzeiro. Estamos longe dos anos 80, mas Vice City ainda é a capital do sol e da diversão da América. A vida neste arquipélago tropical não é chamativa, mas é boa. Pegue uma cervejinha e puxe uma cadeira de praia, mas tome cuidado, você está à beira das águas mais belas e perigosas da América. Você nunca sabe o que está sob a superfície desta região primordial. Os jacarés podem ser a atração mais famosa, mas há predadores bem mais perigosos e descobertas mais estranhas entre o manguezal. Motéis baratos, atrações fechadas, e galerias de lojas vazias e abandonadas não vão trazer os turistas de volta, mas há uma nova economia neste local que já foi um ponto turístico. Agora mandam o as bebidas baratas, remédios contra a dor e bebidas energéticas. No coração de Leonida, a indústria Americana e os antigos valores ainda reinam supremos, seja qual for o custo. A refinaria de açúcar Allied Crystal providencia os empregos, e a gangue de motociclistas local providencia quase todo o resto. Um marco nacional na fronteira norte do estado, Mount Kalaga oferece as melhores trilhas off-road e pontos de pesca e caça. Nas florestas em torno, caipiras místicos e radicais paranóicos vivem longe dos olhos vigilantes do governo. Com estações de Rock Clássico, Hip-Hop Moderno, Pop, Metal, Dance, Latina, Anos 80, Electrônica, Blues, Baladas, Talk Radio, e muito mais, Grand Theft Auto VI possui a maior e mais variada seleção de rádios em um jogo até hoje. Além disso, pela primeira vez, Grand Theft Auto VI apresenta uma série de podcasts sob demanda para Jason e Lucia ouvirem além das rádios de Leonida, com ambos disponíveis para ouvir em veículos e a pé usando fones de ouvido e earbuds conectados aos seus smartphones.

sources.title: Jason's stoic character in Grand Theft Auto 6 was inspired by Steve McQueen and research into Army veterans: 'These guys typically aren't running their mouths'
sources.text: Rockstar made a point of creating "authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality." It's already clear that Grand Theft Auto 6 has a very different timbre than most other GTA games. While criminal hijinks and acerbic satire remain part of the experience, it's also much more interested in portraying characters and relationships in a more convincing, human fashion. One of the most striking examples of this is its depiction of co-protagonist Jason Duval, who, unlike the vast majority of GTA's main characters, is often notable for what he doesn't say rather than what he does. According to Rockstar's senior vice president of narrative Rupert Humphries, Jason's laconic nature was inspired by a personality type observed in both cinema and real-life. "When we decided we wanted to tell a story about a couple on the run, we looked at all the similar kinds of movies, and one of the ones that really stood out was [Sam] Peckinpah's The Getaway" Humphries explained in a statement given to Destructoid (via GamesRadar ). Steve McQueen was famous for pulling lines out of scripts and saying things with his presence alone. We wanted to see how close we could get to that with a game character, where so many of our protagonists have been the opposite." Humphries says this also "resonated" with research the studio was doing around Army veterans, particularly Army Rangers. In Grand Theft Auto 6 , Duval is a veteran of the game's equivalent military organisation called the Marauders. "These guys typically aren't running their mouths or reacting to something unless it's strictly necessary, while still being strong and still asserting themselves," Humphries explained. Establishing a more grounded character was not solely a directive for Jason. It was a goal of the writing more broadly. This is interesting considering Florida was picked as the setting for GTA 6 in-part due to the wild 'Florida Man' stories that circulate on the Internet from the state. "Researching the prolific and headline-grabbing criminal activity that had been taking place over decades in Florida was an obvious starting point," game writer Michael Wiafe pointed out. "From then on, it was about coming up with authentic characters that didn't stray too far from reality but also were not totally bound by it either," Wiafe continues. "The majority of our main characters are undeniably reprehensible on paper, full-blown criminals, but also decent human beings. Their moral makeup isn’t necessarily cut-and-dry, and we don’t attempt to make excuses for them. What's important is how they resonate, no matter where you're experiencing the game in the world." This is just one of the things that makes Rockstar's latest crime sim a marvel on pretty much all fronts . And while us PC gamers will have to wait an unspecified amount of time before it arrives on the platform, you can bet it going to be quite the experience when it does. sources.title: Grand Theft Auto 6 has a 'complex drug network' that tracks everything from where drugs come from to 'how they eventually reach the street-level buyer'
sources.text: "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real." I've only dipped my toe into Grand Theft Auto 6 thus far, but I'm already impressed by the detail Rockstar has baked into its world. One thing I'm always curious about with games like this, however, is how much of that detail is on the surface versus what's actually happening under the hood. I'm still too early in the game to judge this for myself, but according to Rockstar, there is way more going on in terms of how NPCs behave than players will ever likely see. One striking example of this is how GTA 6 's gang compounds conduct their drug operations. In an interview with IGN , Rockstar's senior design director for its open world Steven Messinger explained that GTA 6 fully simulates drug distribution from top to bottom. "A big part of [the open world's design] was establishing deep backstories for almost everything, even if they were never meant to be fully explained to the player, and then really sticking to those backstories," Messinger pointed out. "For example, our gang compounds have a complex drug network we've fully mapped out: where the drugs come from, who brings them in and how, how they're distributed to each compound, what happens at each stop, and how they eventually reach the street-level buyer." Messinger notes that "players will only pick up bits and pieces of this". But representing this process wholesale means that, when players do notice it, it always feels authentic and believable. "Having that structure in the background as something we consistently refer to helps everything feel more real, like this big machine is always running even when players aren't there." While this may only be designed for players to notice passively, I'm now keen to follow this system and see just how consistently it holds up. sources.title: GTA 6: Find and break into Freddie Gibbs’ doomsday compound in Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: How to find Freddie Gibbs, enter his compound, and get rewards in Grand Theft Auto 6 Rapper Freddie Gibbs is in Grand Theft Auto 6, and heâs a doomsday prepper with an impressive compound and bunker. Freddie is convinced that the apocalypse is coming, so heâs built up a doomsday bunker and compound, complete with an electric fence, mines, and even explosive drones. Thatâs just the defenses â heâs really prepared for the world to end. Freddie is a pretty nice and generous guy once you get to know him, but getting to know him isnât so easy. In this guide, weâre breaking down how to find and break into Freddieâs compound both times in GTA 6. Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Freddieâs compound is located on the North shore of Lake Leonida in North Leonard County. Itâs on the same road as One-Eyed Willieâs Auto Shop (Ultimate Edition exclusive). You canât miss it as itâs a large compound surrounded by electric fences, and has multiple billboards propped up warning about the end of the world. The first time you break into Freddieâs compound, it has an obvious flaw. A water tower to the rear of the compound is outside of the electric fence. It has an unblocked ladder that you can climb to take you up to a platform, from which you can jump onto the roof of a shed inside the electric fence. You will have to watch out for both proximity mines and drones. Proximity mines will be highlighted in Focus mode, and when you hear a drone, Focus mode will again give you enough time to shoot them down. The best route through the compound is sticking close to the fence while heading East, and then South. Proximity mines will not be placed on the pipes and cables in the compound, meaning you can use them as a walkway. You will complete the challenge by getting to the front door of the large dug-out bunker. The first time you complete this challenge, Freddie will free you and challenge you to return later, after he improves his defenses. After some time, Freddie will text Jason and Lucia, challenging them to a rematch. You need to break into his compound and get to the door of his bunker again, only this time the water tower isnât an option, and the proximity mines and drones have been buffed. Nothing is impossible, though, and Jason and Lucia are both pretty good climbers who are able to clamber on top of large vehicles. You see where this is going. To the rear of the compound â the Northwest corner â youâll find a tractor with a large trailer, along with a bulldozer. Park the tractor and trailer along the fence, and then use the bulldozer to lift the trailer into the air. This will give you the perfect ramp to climb up the tractor, onto the trailer, and over the electric fence. Even Freddie wonât see it coming. Head to the bunker door again with the same route as last time â while watching out for more mines â and Freddie will finally emerge to greet you before inviting you inside. A storm will start, and you will have to choose between staying or leaving. If you leave, Freddie will give you $6,250 cash. As a reward for staying with him, Freddie will give you the valuable Benefactor Dubsta that you can register and keep.

sources.title: GTA 6: Recover Jason’s stash from Key Lento in Grand Theft Auto 6
sources.text: How to recover Jason’s Key Lento Rainy-Day Fund stash in Grand Theft Auto 6 Mild spoiler alert: you should at least make it to Chapter 2 of Grand Theft Auto 6 before reading on. Things go very wrong at the climax of GTA 6âs first chapter. Jason and Lucia will have to abandon their home in Key Lento, and the stash of cash and Jasonâs collection of photographs go with them. But you can go back. The stash under the floorboards has burned up, but the money and photographs in the metal box are still intact, and you can recover them. Only, thatâs easier said than done. In this guide, weâre breaking down the best way to recover Jasonâs stash and photographs in Grand Theft Auto 6 . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. To reiterate the above: the money you stashed under the floorboards will have burned up, but Jason did put $5,000 away as a Rainy-Day Fund for his family. If you stored more than that under the floorboards, Iâm sorry to say that the money is sadly gone. Still, the $5,000 is worth recovering, and thereâs at least one nice surprise to see. Your stash is, of course, in the same building that burned up in Key Lento. Cops will be patrolling the nearby area, and theyâll be stationed in front of Jasonâs house and on the dock around back, meaning you canât simply drive up in either a car or boat. The best option is to get a RydeMe taxi to a nearby location on the North or East side of the zone the cops are patrolling, like Chuckâs Tackle and Shot or The Rusty Anchor. Make sure to wear a disguise â hat, sunglasses, bandana â and sneak through gardens to get to the building North of Jasonâs burned-out home, just over the small canal where boats can dock. Cops wonât be patrolling this side of the house, meaning you can dive into the water and swim over to the boat ramp near Jasonâs basketball hoop. The stairs immediately in front of the ramp are very close to a pair of cops out front, so circle around the North side of the house and use the other stairs. If you stop to look under the stairs, youâll find Jasonâs snake Dolores has made a nest and laid some eggs. A happy ending. Climbing the stairs, youâll easily be able to find the stash and metal tin in the same place as ever. Quickly recover both the money and photographs, and escape the same way you came in before getting outside of the patrol zone and changing your disguise. Congratulations, youâve got some of your money back.

sources.title: GTA 6 has a 99 Metascore from critics, but players are review bombing it
sources.text: Grand Theft Auto 6 might be one of the best-reviewed games of all time, but you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score. While critics have given Rockstar's latest a Metascore of 99, its user score has dropped to 5.6 out of 10 at the time of writing, which Metacritic classifies as "mixed or average". Of the 54,000+ ratings left, 44 percent are "negative". The score had previously dropped into the red, but has since recovered a little. Some negative reviews raise genuine complaints, such as the game's 30FPS cap on console, while others take issue with how much of the story focuses on Jason and Lucia's relationship instead of the crime-spree antics of past games. "Expectations might've killed this game," states one 0/10 review. "The hype that something otherworldly would come to be flopped. The hyperrealism makes it feel slow, mundane and boring. Its a tecnichal [sic] advancement for sure but for the wrong reasons. Goodlooks zero personality type stuff. Its not as edgy as the rest of the gta games. And thats exactly my problem like is not funny. The game gets carried by its visuals and radio stations. Certain limitations make it feel like not gta and new features make it feel like not gta. In the end it feels like a life simulator and the point of gaming is to escape from reality." "Genuinely hated almost every minute of this experience," wrote another. "After years of waiting and an absurd amount of hype, GTA VI somehow managed to leave me more frustrated than entertained. The excessive sexual content gets exhausting, and instead of adding anything meaningful to the experience, it often feels like Rockstar is desperately trying to shock its audience. "The story is painfully disappointing, the writing fails to keep me invested, and I honestly couldn't care less about what happens to most of these **** gameplay isn't doing the game any favours either. Glitches, bugs, annoying inconsistencies, and frustrating moments constantly get in the way of actually enjoying the experience. It's ridiculous that a game of this scale, backed by a studio with Rockstar's resources, can feel this rough. I expected a polished experience, not a glorified debugging ****." Others point to "woke" and "DEI" agendas. "A major step down in the writing department compared to previous instalments coupled with the obvious DEI-fication, unfun realism and the resulting player freedom restrictions leave a sour taste in the otherwise detailed gorgeous open world," said one reviewer. Another unhappy player wrote: "Shameful DEI hijacked cuck simulator, the most overrated game of all time and it's not even close." GTA 6 launched on Thursday for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. Earlier today, actor Jesse James Rose revealed the game features the series' first non-binary character . Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review . And if you need some help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats .

sources.title: GTA 6 Is Getting Review Bombed in Zelda vs. GTA Troll War
sources.text: Soulcalibur catches strays in Metacritic feud Grand Theft Auto 6 may be the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic , and may have earned a record-breaking $3.79 billion on launch day , but that doesn't mean Rockstar Games' new blockbuster can't have its haters. Multiple groups have descended on GTA 6 's Metacritic page to attack the game for its perceived shortcomings, much of that criticism is based on culture war nonsense. But some of GTA 6 's detractors are targeting the game for another reason: for slighting The Legend of Zelda. GTA 6 made its debut on Metacritic with a 99 Metascore , based on more than 150 critics reviews. That feat nudged the previous best game of all time, at least going by Metacritic score averages, The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time , down to No. 2 on the review aggregator website. That has led some Legend of Zelda supporters to review bomb Grand Theft Auto 6 on Metacritic, and some GTA 6 supporters to do the same to Zelda. Now, both camps are in a pointless war to lower the other franchise's user review score. Over the past few days, GTA and Zelda fans have been trading barbs and slinging "0" user review scores at their perceived rivals. As of Sunday, Nov. 22, Grand Theft Auto 6 's user review score on Metacritic has dipped to 5.6, indicating "mixed or average" reviews from players. In response, the original Ocarina of Time and its Nintendo Switch 2 remake have also been review bombed (though their user scores are in the mid-8s as of Sunday). Unsurprisingly, the discourse around this pointless feud has not been particularly intelligent. Each camp is simply trying to drive down its rivals’ user score, with supporters writing the bare minimum in their user "reviews" — often with plenty of typos. Even poor Soulcalibur , the 1999 fighting game released on Dreamcast, is catching strays amid the fighting. Some GTA 6 supporters are now wading into Soulcalibur 's user reviews, slamming Bandai Namco's weapons-based fighter for no good reason beyond its ranking as the third-best game of all time according to Metacritic's algorithm. Grand Theft Auto 6 's detractors aren't just misguided Zelda fans. Unsurprisingly, a contingent of GTA fans are attacking the game for its perceived "wokeness" amid more legitimate concerns about performance. "30 FPS, Concole Exclusive, Restricted freedom and uninteresting characters are a no go for a 13 year development cycle," reads one recent negative review of GTA 6 . Much of the feedback, however, seems to focus on having a female co-lead character and game mechanics that ask players to be considerate toward her . "In GTA6 you need to do chores, pick up an abusive girl from prison and then do more chores. Boring characters, boring missions and 30fps cap. I would have rather burned that $100 than giving it to the woke garbage R* has become," reads one scathing review. "15 years for this dissapointing cuck simulator. Rip rockstar. You were my childhood," reads another. "Game is straight woke trash," another troll says. The tenor of GTA 6 's negative reviews isn't much different from the trollish feedback infesting reviews of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, surprisingly. "THEY MADE LINK A CUCK IN THIS GAME!!!!! ALWAYS DOING WHAT HIS FEMALE FAIRY NAVI TELLS HIM WHAT TO DO!!!! CRITICS PROVE ONCE AGAIN THEY’VE BEEN BOUGHT OFF!!!!!" reads one of the many negative reviews to invoke cuck simulator language. While this kind of petty squabbling is par for the course in internet discourse, especially in the video game sphere, at least fans of both The Legend of Zelda and Grand Theft Auto can take comfort in knowing that both franchises have great games to enjoy in 2026. And that, if you're reading this, you're likely not spending your time fighting in the Metacritic comments.

sources.title: As GTA 6 gets review-bombed on Metacritic, GTA fans have started review-bombing Ocarina of Time in response
sources.text: The year’s two best games are currently being bombarded with negative reviews A civil war of sorts has broken out among Metacritic’s user scores, with players downvoting numerous high-profile games. Grand Theft Auto 6 was already being review-bombed by users before the game had even been released, with Metacritic removing these reviews and implementing its typical wait period, where user reviews can’t be submitted until at least 36 hours after the game’s release. Now that window has closed and reviews can be submitted, the review-bombing has continued , with GTA 6 receiving more than 10,000 reviews at the time of writing, with a user score of just 5.6 out of 10. Given that the game currently sits at a Metacritic score of 99 and sits top of the site’s Best Games of All Time list, the fact that so many people are scoring the game 0 could be considered suspicious at best. Many of the 0-scoring reviews appear to stem from players’ disappointment that GTA 6 is, in their eyes, a “relationship simulator” where the aim is to keep Lucia happy, something that seemingly doesn’t sit well with some of the audience. “This does not hold a candle to GTA 5 and deserve all criticism especially it being a cuck simulator,” reads one 2/10 review. Another 0/10 review reads: “GTA Feminist. Once again, the woke movement turns the game into a just feminist product.” On the other side of the fence, GTA fans have started review-bombing The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake, which until recently had the highest Metacritic user score of all time following its own successful launch (its professional Metacritic score currently stands at 95). While the Ocarina of Time remake’s user score still stands at 8.3, this is mainly to the tens of thousands of positive reviews it received after its release. In the past few days it’s suddenly been hit with an onslaught of 0 scores, some of which explicitly saying they’re from GTA fans who believe their game’s review-bombing was being done by Zelda fans. “I saw a guy giving a Rockstar game a 0 and saying the company was crap and that Nintendo was the King of Games, so to compensate for the negative review of the Rockstar game I came here to make the same sad and immature comment,” wrote one 0/10 score. “This game is what nostalgia is about â people loving this boring ass game because of nostalgia and FOMO,” wrote another 0/10. “It’s just another game like other ones. No hate for Zelda, but Zelda fans that went to GTA 6 reviews to hate, I’m hating them back, sorry for the people that didn’t do that.” The same has been happening to other games at the top of Metacritic’s Best Games of All Time list, including the original 1998 version of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, with GTA fans review-bombing them too. “Fine, since you want to play dirty,” reads one 0/10 review posted this week for the N64 original. “As many of you who didnât ever play GTA 6 and give it 0 just for 1st place, then why canât I.” “For GTA 6 , child, you are starting a war,” reads a 0/10 review posted for Dreamcast fighting game SoulCalibur, currently number 3 in Metacritic’s all-time list. “Wait for it, Jason’s nail will bury you, kid, wait for it.” The trend will call into further question the validity of user scores on Metacritic, which are often accused of being hijacked by player bases using it as a tool to further an agenda. Earlier this year Splatoon Raiders saw the opposite of review-bombing, as fans of the series showered it with scores of 10 to make it t he seventh best-scoring game of all time on the site. This too should be taken with numerous caveats in mind, as this list is usually an indication of popularity (or notoriety) rather than quality. According to the same list, Disneyâs Nintendo DS title Cory in the House is the joint-second-greatest video game of all time, almost certainly because it became a meme and users scored it 10 in numerous joke reviews. User scores on the site also have a habit of skewing heavily to either 10 or 0, as users attempt to make the biggest impact on the overall score. Indeed, while Splatoon Raiders has received hundreds of 10 scores from users, it also has some 0 scores from users seemingly trying to bring its User Score down.

sources.text: Warning: this story features spoilers for an optional side activity. Those two chilling words were so soft I wondered if I'd heard them correctly – after all, the only souls in this orchard were me and Tootsie, an escaped cow draped in red cloth with a rosette stuck to her forehead. But no, I had heard them, and I turned them over in my head as I led Tootsie back along her rampaging path, through fallen fruit, over a busted wooden fence, and to her owner, a dairy farmer I'd found on the side of the road, flustered and crying about his prized $2 million show cow. I was still processing those two words as we approached the farmer's trailer, and when he told me that tonight, a fan had paid to watch a private Tootsie mud bath, I knew what I had to do. I shooed her to her freedom – "Go, run! Live your best life!" – and she galloped, ribbons fluttering, hooves pounding into the distance. To freedom rather than a busy highway, I hoped. I was Jason, the good Samaritan (if you ignore the part where I then provoked the farmer to start a fight, knocked him out cold, stamped on his limp body and stole the $500 in his pocket). This was about six hours into Rockstar's latest masterpiece . For a game as vast and open as GTA 6 , I found the opening strangely claustrophobic – to begin, the giant map of Leonida is shrouded in fog apart from the sliver of the Florida Keys where Jason lives and some surrounding swamp land. Key Lento is so dense with activities, shops, missions, and random encounters, not to mention the constant distraction of pottering around Jason's waterside house, that I felt overwhelmed by it all. And so, perhaps earlier than the game wanted me to, I pointed Jason's red pickup north and started driving. What I found was that GTA 6's open world holds delights that you can enjoy no matter where you are in the main story. I slipped west of Vice City, turning off the highway's spiralling spaghetti junctions near Buckskin Swamp. Soon I parked up at Emerald Springs, a nature reserve with pristine boardwalks and stands selling orange juice and doughnuts. I plodded the planks, eating a sandwich from the Black Bear Deli. I studied some ducks, beat up an entitled British tourist, stole a bike, and pedalled back to my car. I had hoped to find something crafted and scripted, but the fact that I could still have fun in a place with ostensibly nothing to do fills me with hope for the rest of the game. It was stark how, in just a few minutes of driving from Key Lento, the atmosphere had shifted completely, from road rage to tranquility. The beauty of the place and the amusing conversations to eavesdrop were captivating, even without a weird or wonderful encounter. I placed another waypoint vaguely northeast. It was on the way that I met Tootsie for what was undoubtedly the strangest moment I've had so far in GTA 6. Not only did it imply that animals could talk in this world, or at least psychically communicate, but that Jason could hear them. I wonder if that means anything. My detour from the main story had been worth it for Tootise (and the $500 from her owner) but it was barely lunchtime. GTA 6's extended day-night cycle feels central to how you play: you can get so much more done in a day than in Red Dead Redemption 2, and even after a languid morning routine of working out and coffee, you're still out the door before 08:00am. Low on gas, I rolled into a forecourt in Ambrosia, a town where abandoned factories and containers made way for quaint high streets. I was rewarded with another unique scene. A chap with a camo shirt and teeth like a Donegal graveyard spraying gasoline into a bathtub inexplicably mounted in the back of his pickup. "None of your regulations or mind control is going to stop me!" he shouted as the liquid sloshed down his tailgate, coating the dozen bumper stickers and dripping onto his boots. "I can pump gasoline wherever I want." He even sprayed it on Jason, and it took the threat of nearby sirens to hold me back. Thankfully, his cigarette did the work instead, falling and lighting the gas on fire, the flames engulfing his feet. "Those cigarettes'll kill ya man," Jason said, smirking. Every scripted random encounter so far has felt deliciously crafted. Some funny, some nightmarish. I like that they vary in length and level of interactivity so that when one starts, you never know if it'll trigger an actual quest or just puff into nothingness. I could've just watched the gas station spectacle unfold, like a mini stage play, but hours later when I found a tiger mauling bodies in an abandoned swamp hotel, I had to act. Later, I ambled a row of cafes and restaurants, got a haircut, ate a protein bar, and threw the protein bar wrapper at a guy who looked at me funny, sparking a seven-person brawl that drew the attention of a cops and – when I gunned one officer down – a police chopper. I was forced to flee even further north, driving along some railtracks and into the wilderness, not able to stop at the wonderfully named Thrillbully Mud Club. I eventually lost the police chopper and looped back to Ambrosia as the sun dawdled. I wanted to get back by bedtime but I didn't fancy the seven-mile drive back to Key Lento, and as if Rockstar was reading my thoughts, the next corner I rounded revealed a hospital complete with a helipad. I climbed into the cockpit, apologising silently to the next poor sod who needed airlifting to safety, and flew south. I could have seen this all later in the game. And perhaps I would have gotten more out of it if I'd waited another six hours: I haven't yet done a full robbery, and I'm sure Ambrosia is littered with potential targets. I've only controlled Lucia for one mission, and I'd love to see what happens if both protagonists find something strange together. But the day of distractions, a break from quests, was exactly what I needed, and I was feeling glad that Rockstar doesn't restrict where you can go from the start. I realise that "go and explore" is

sources.title: Should you shake Mattia's hand in GTA 6?
sources.text: Shaking Mattia's hand seems like quite an important moment in GTA 6 The chance to shake Mattia's hand in GTA 6 comes up right at the start of the mission Day Release, seemingly like a key decision that might affect the tone of the rest of the mission and future job prospects. Multiple GamesRadar+ writers have gone through both options, and it's a lot less important of a decision in GTA 6 than you think, so here's what we know about the significance of shaking Mattia's hand. Be aware of some very mild spoilers for later missions in Chapter 1 below. Shaking Mattia's hand in GTA 6 makes no difference to any events in the Day Release mission . If you shake his hand, you shake his hand, and if you don't, you don't. Mattia doesn't even acknowledge that you left him hanging. Later in the mission, Mattia offers Jason and Lucia some drugs in a nightclub and, again, accepting or refusing has no clear repercussions. Comparing videos of the choices side-by-side, there were no obvious differences between either outcome as the same thing happens regardless - Mattia either takes the drugs back or hands them over, stands up and leaves, then Jason and Lucia take to the dancefloor. The rest of the mission then plays out as normal. As far as I can tell, turning Mattia down in either of these situations in Day Release has no long-term impact either as the "job" that he mentions at the end of the mission is critical to the story and can't be avoided. Just make sure you've done everything before the GTA 6 Tourist Trap mission as it's an important one – and if you get stuck, my GTA 6 Tourist Trap walkthrough can help. sources.text: If you want to get in and out of a heist as fast as possible, here's how to get GTA 6 safe codes Finding and inputting GTA 6 safe codes is a slicker way to break into the 50+ safes scattered throughout the GTA 6 map . While some safes can be opened with sheer brute force, those that require a code often offer more lucrative rewards, so finding these safe codes can be a great way to make cash fast in GTA 6 . Unfortunately, these safe codes aren't always easy to come by. While some of the safe codes in GTA 6 are set – with those critical to the story and major side missions always consisting of the same digits– many of the codes are randomized and can change from player to player. So, while I can't give you the codes for those safes, I can at least help by guiding you on how to obtain them. So read on for tips on finding these randomized safe codes and for a list of set safe codes and their locations. There are two methods of getting GTA 6 safe codes: Which you'll need depends on the location, but by using your Focus by pressing down on L3 and R3/LS and RS, you can highlight the location of the safe code if there is one. If you can't see one, you probably need to threaten the staff by holding down the LT/L2 button and then press X/Square to threaten. Eventually, the threaten option will turn into a 'Safe code?' option, as seen in the image above. The Avery Pawn Shop GTA 6 safe code is an example of one of these, so why not use that to try it out. Alternatively, safes that require a code can be blown open using sticky bombs . These are only unlocked once you reach the Credit Checked mission in Chapter 3, but as I've explained in my dedicated guide to getting into the Kingpin Bowling safe in GTA 6 , there are a few you can pick up at the alley - and presumably other places around Leonida - before you unlock them at Ammu-Nation. These are the set GTA 6 safe codes that are the same for every player: Aside from the 0420 safe code that's given to you in Chapter 1, there are three main safe codes you'll need when gathering funds in GTA 6, and they're all related to the Kolt gang in Port Gellhorn. All three codes are found in the same place, Brooks Boatworks, but since they're set, you can use them from our list above without having to go looking for them. This won't save you a lot of trouble, though, as you'll still have to get past the gang in all three locations anyway. sources.text: Wondering where to find the DWNPLY sneakers and get them for free in the Ride of Die mission? Ride or Die mission sees Jason team up with his pal Dre’Quan to pull off a high-stakes car/fancy shoes theft.Â Here’s how to complete the GTA 6 Ride or Die mission, including where to find the sneakers, how to get them for free and how to steal DWNPLY’s car. This Ride or Die walkthrough is one of dozens ofÂ GTA 6 guides we’ve published since the game launched. Check them all out in our GTA 6 Guide Hub . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Ride or Die becomes available in Chapter 3 after completing Credit Check. Around a day later, Dre’Quan will message Jason and ask him to meet outside the Jack of Hearts club in Crosstown. You can only start this mission as Jason. If you approach the mission start with Lucia, the mission will be locked out, and you’ll have to wait and come back later as just Jason. Sit on the ledge outside and wait for Dre’Quan to appear. He’ll tell you about his plan to steal DWNPLY’s car, but in order to do that, Jason and Dre’Quan will have to get close to him. The best way to do this is to get to DWNPLY’s sneaker launch at the Eris store. After the chat, follow him to the Eris store on the Downtown waterfront. There are several different ways you can get the DWNPLY sneakers. One option is to find the couple pictured in the image above, that are taking a photo. Speak to them, and then eventually they’ll leave the store. After they walk far enough away, you can rob them. If you do this, you have to make sure you weren’t spotted, and that it wasn’t reported to the police, or it will cause the mission to fail. You can also buy the sneakers for a scalper that is hanging around the shop. This costs over $1000 and is not worth it, especially when you can easily steal them. Head up to the top floor, and look for the door in the image above. There will be an NPC in a pink dress standing near it. As long as there are no staff around (they walk around the floor in shifts, so just wait if one is close) you can walk straight through this door. Behind the door you’ll find a staff break room. Here you can walk over to a pair of the sneakers that are sitting in a bag near a table. If you’re struggling to find them, check the image below and match it in-game. Now that you have the sneakers, head back downstairs in the Eris store and speak to Dre’Quan, who will be waiting just beyond the entrance. Follow him upstairs towards the VIP lounge. A bouncer will initially block your way, but look at him and select the Show Shoes interaction. Showing the DWNPLY sneakers allows Jason to enter without paying. Once inside the VIP lounge, head towards the left of the bar to find DWNPLY sitting with a group of people.Approach him and hand over the sneakers. While he’s signing them, hold the triangle interaction button to reach for his car keys. He’ll interrupt Jason to ask who the signature is for. Answer his question, then continue holding the button until Jason successfully takes the keys. Follow Dre’Quan downstairs and head towards the parking garage. Use the car horn prompt to locate DWNPLY’s vehicle. Follow the sound towards the eastern side of the parking lot, where you’ll find the car in a lit VIP parking space. The parking space glows green, so you should be able to see it from far across the parking garage.Â As you leave, a gang member will jump onto the bonnet. Swerve from side to side to throw him off before driving towards the Stockyard Speedshop. Alternatively, you can do what I did and take a jump at a ridiculous angle and the bodyguard will take off into space. Then, DWNPLY’s bodyguard and his gang will pursue you. Escape the red search area on your minimap before continuing to the Speedshop. Completing Ride or Die doesn’t provide any rewards. Not even the shoes.

sources.text: Where where to find and start The Final Flush mission in GTA 6 and earn a stamina upgrade The Big Flush in GTA 6 is an optional mission, but it's well worth your time for a permanent stamina upgrade. You can start this GTA 6 mission from Chapter 1 onwards, and once it's done it's incredibly useful reward will allow you to do energy-draining activities, like running and swimming, for longer. It's also just a fun side mission to do. After finding an odd poster in a men's bathroom stall, you are enlisted to help oddball Dr. Merle to prove his bizarre conspiracy theory that the government is stealing DNA from poop (which is seemingly based on a real report about Putin ) and things only get stranger from there. To start The Final Flush mission in GTA 6, go to the bathroom block toward the north tip of Corsair Key in Mariana County (just north-east of Key Lento). It should be easy to find as it's the only building in Corsair Key. Enter the men's toilet and you'll see a handmade poster on the wall that says "Stop! Don't Flush. Scan to learn the truth #NOFLUSHERS" with a QR code attached. Use your WaiNK IT app to scan the code and you'll receive a message from an Automated Machine that tells you to reply "TRUTH" to join the No Flushers movement. Select the "Truth" reply and you'll receive another message telling you that whoever is messaging will be at Frank's Waffles in Vice City. If asked, you need to repeat the code: 00-00-02. You need to meet the mystery No Flusher at Frank's Waffles in the Tequesta neighborhood of Vice City, in Vice-Dale County. When you enter the waffle house, you'll find a man muttering to himself in one of the booths nearest the toilets. However, he seemingly won't appear if it's not night time, as, when I went during the day, the mission icon had a padlock on it and the man wasn't there. When you get near the man, he covers up whatever he's working on and tells you that he's holding a royal flush. When he asks do you have a "coda for that?," hold LT/LR while looking at the man to bring up the dialogue menu and select the code option with X/A. The oddball man is Dr. Merle, who quickly ingests a tracking device and begins waffling (no pun intended) about his conspiracy theory that the poop of Leonida citizens isn't actually going to the sewers but is instead going to a secret government DNA siphoning center. He then goes to the corporate-controlled bathroom to deposit the tracking device into the federally-controlled sewers, so you can track where Leonida's bowel movements go to the source of the whole operation. Once Dr Merle is done in the bathroom, follow him to his van outside. Follow his verbal directions to follow the tracker and it'll take you to the sewage treatment plant in Hamlet in Vice-Dale County. Follow the waypoint to park the van on the coast then follow Dr Merle on foot to the plant. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more When you reach the plant's fence, Dr. Merle begins unlocking a metal gate so that you can get inside and asks you to keep an eye out. Keep an eye on the road on the other side of the gate as a van will soon approach. If the driver stops and asks what you're doing, the best approach is to use the "Defuse" dialogue option to tell the worker you're simply fixing the gate. Once you're inside the sewage treatment plant ground, you're tasked with finding the tracker. The best approach is to head toward the area highlighted pink on your GTA 6 map until you see the two works chatting. Approach them and, when asked if you are electricians, use the "Lie" dialogue option to go along with their theory. Go through the open metal gate to the left of the works, then slightly right and you'll see a set of double doors. Enter these doors to enter the facility. Once you get inside Dr. Merle starts to freak out because the tracking device is apparently below your feet, but there's no obvious way to reach it, so he asks you to find a way down. Go up the metal stairs in this room and you'll find a control panel on the platform above. Select Triangle/Y to interact with the panel. To open the stairs that lead downstairs, all three lights on the left of the control panel need to be turned to green. So, push the buttons next to the two red lights (the middle and bottom ones), to turn them green, then tilt the main lever on the panel. A secret staircase leading downstairs will then open up where Dr.Merle is sitting. Go down the stairs and you'll enter a room with a large, mysterious-looking chamber. Determined to prove his DNS-siphoning theory is correct, Dr. Merle gets into the chamber– which soon begins to fill with liquid – and asks you to flush him. Press the red button on the control panel in front of the chamber to do so. Unfortunately, this puts the water authority on your case. They warn over a loudspeaker that the authorities are on their way and that the chamber is highly toxic, so you absolutely should not step inside it. Step inside the chamber and you'll automatically be flushed. You wake up (somehow) outside Jason's House with a notification telling you your max stamina has increased. © GamesRadar+. sources.text: Mami Knows Best is the fortieth mission in GTA 6. In the Mami Knows Best mission, Lucia reunites with her mother, Mia,Â as Mia shows off her new job. Things quickly go poorly. Here’s how to complete the Mami Knows Best mission in GTA 6, including all objectives and the rewards you can earn. Need more GTA 6 guides? Then check out our GTA 6 Guide Hub . Guides: If you're playing Grand Theft Auto 6, make sure to checkÂ out ourÂ complete walkthrough hub , featuringÂ beginner tips , navigation experience explained , GTA 6 cheats , and more. Mami Knows Best is a Chapter 3 story mission that can only be started when playing as Lucia. It becomes available after completing Dealer’s Choice as Jason and Lucia. Meet Lucia’s mum, Mia Caminos. After the initial conversation about Mia’s real estate business, get into her car and drive to her new property in Hamlet. Follow Mia inside the house and explore each room as she inspects the property. It’s an absolute wreck, and you may have noticed. Once you’ve finished looking around, return towards the entrance and help Mia up when prompted. Next, head outside and start clearing the front lawn. Pick up the rubbish and throw each item to the blue dumpster. After you do this a few times, the objective will change to help Mia in the backyard. Follow Mia around to the backyard, where you’ll find a mattress floating in the swimming pool. Interact with it and follow the button prompts to pull it out. Be ready for trouble, however. An alligator jumps out of the pool attacks Mia, grabbing her leg. Quickly pull out your weapon and shoot the animal to save her. If you fail to do this, Mia will be eaten, and the mission will fail. Use Focus Mode and target the red areas onÂ the alligator to ensure you kill it. After this, the M7 gang, who own the property, turn up. Following a confrontation with the gang, Mia decides to get even with her new neighbours. Cross the street and climb into the excavator. Drive it towards the gang’s property and start destroying the house and vehicles parked in the driveway. Most of the house is fully destructable, so I’d reccomend grabbing the roof and other bits that can be easly torn off. Don’t forget the cars.Â Keep causing damage until the objective updates. Once you’ve caused enough destruction, return to Mia’s car and get inside. Drive her to the office which is close to the neighbourhood, and that’s you done with Mami Knows Best. There is no cash payment, weapon or vehicle reward for completing this mission. Just a mother’s appreciation, which is priceless.

sources.title: GTA 6 Players Report Crashes on PS5 With Error CE-108255-1
sources.text: GTA 6 players on PlayStation 5 have reported frequent crashes tied to error code CE-108255-1, and it looks like it's blocking them from progressing through the story while they wait for Sony and Rockstar to send out a fix. Although Rockstar Games spent a decade making its new Grand Theft Auto game, it's no surprise to see the new highest-rated game of all time launching with at least a few hiccups. Some have it worse than others, though, with more than a few reports of crashes affecting PS5 consoles popping up online in the days following GTA 6's launch. The most common cause seems to be tied to error code CE-108255-1, which, as defined by Sony , simply indicates that "an error occurred with the game/application." It seems that, although the majority of players aren't encountering the issue, those who have haven't been able to find a proper fix. Adding to the trouble is that those who have met these dreaded GTA 6 crashes are getting them pretty frequently, and what's triggering them isn't always clear. There are reports from players on both standard PS5 and PS5 Pro consoles running into these issues, with some even saying that crashes appear to be tied to the story, barring them from making any progress. "I've noticed that the issue manifests differently for different players," one Reddit user said . "In my case, the game crashes on Jason's loading screen: it freezes and then displays the CE-108255-1 error code, meaning I can't even get into the game. Others manage to play for a few minutes before experiencing a crash. I really hope Sony and Rockstar work together to investigate and resolve this issue as soon as possible." Game crashes are annoying for anyone, but when a massive game like GTA 6, which many feel has a less-than-generous autosave system , suddenly boots players back to the PS5 home screen without warning, it can be especially troublesome. Many who have reported the crashes to PlayStation Support say they've been directed to Rockstar, while those who report to Rockstar say they're being directed to PlayStation. One player said they feel like they're "stuck in an endless support loop, with a game I paid for and still can't play." Meanwhile, those who have managed to get help say most assistance hasn't been able to completely resolve their issues. However, some have said they've had luck with a few tried-and-true methods, such as uninstalling and reinstalling the game, making sure both the PS5 and game have their most recent updates, and restoring licenses. "I’ve done everything possible to solve this," another player said . "Deleted cache. Rebuilt database, deleted everything else from my console, took it apart, cleaned it, turned HDR off, switched to 1080p, went and updated game license, deleted and reinstalled and still crashing. Ugh. I’ve got a day 1 PS5 with a disc drive. Other friends of mine with the same console are playing with no issue." Again, it's unclear if the crashing issue is tied specifically to the PS5 or GTA 6 itself. Until either entity comes up with an update, though, all affected players are stuck on launch weekend. GTA 6 released for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19 and, in its first 24 hours, made Rockstar $3.79 billion. It's the most successful launch in the history of entertainment , and although its exact unit sales have yet to be disclosed, parent company Take-Two Interactive was at least willing to share that it sold 32.5 million copies in pre-orders alone.
